parts.text: Which claim correctly places the reflected point $C'$?

options.text: $C'$ is $5\,\mathrm{cm}$ to the left of the line, at the same height as $C$.
$C'$ is the name mirror image for the symmetry line itself.
$C'$ may sit anywhere to the left of the line, at any distance.
$C'$ must stay on the same side of the line as $C$, at $5\,\mathrm{cm}$.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: The diagram shows Gopal completing a mirror image across a fixed vertical symmetry line. Point $C$ is $5\,\mathrm{cm}$ to the right of the line, at a marked height.

part_answers.answer: Reflection across a vertical line keeps height and sends the point the same distance to the opposite side, so C' is 5 cm left at the same height as C.

teacher.key_rationale: Mirror of a point 5 cm right of a vertical line is 5 cm left at the same height. Renaming the line, dropping equal distance, or staying on the same side is wrong.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source into a vertical symmetry line with C 5 cm right and C' 5 cm left.
